note: Benchmark-family surfaces the v0.16.1 generalization audit found in agent packet code and in architecture coverage scoring, with the number of production lines each marker occupies today. They are recorded, not excused. The lint fails on any banned corpus marker outside this inventory, on one more occurrence of a marker inside it, and on any entry that stops matching, so growing or deleting one of these surfaces must edit this file. Every surface must also carry a reason and the issue tracking its deletion; total_markers must equal the number of markers listed below and total_marker_occurrences must equal the sum of their counts, so neither the number of surfaces nor the number of production lines they occupy can move without a reviewable diff that restates both numbers. Twenty-one of the markers below, and two of the counts, were added when the lint stopped reading a Rust lifetime or a possessive apostrophe as an opening string quote: the scanner had been pairing those apostrophes off in file order, so every string literal between one and the next was invisible to it. Those surfaces are not new code, they are code the gate could not see, and they are recorded on the same terms as the rest -- the deletion each file's reason describes now has to cover them too.

pending_claim_profiles.reason: Product claim profiles that still ship without an anti-overfit contract and fixture triple. The registry is versioned data now, so the declaration counted here is the document row, not a Rust constructor. The count is a ratchet: a new profile has to arrive contracted, and migrating one of these has to lower this number and PACKET_CLAIM_PROFILE_PENDING_MIGRATION_RATCHET in the same change. ratchet_ceiling is the high-water the burn-down started from, and burn_down has to account for every profile between the ceiling and the count, so the number can only fall through a stated, evidence-backed migration.

burn_down.evidence: Measured fire triple in packet_claim_profiles: a keyframe claim on a plain stylesheet, a different shared-property claim on a preprocessor sheet, and a measured zero on a layout-only sheet.
Measured fire triple in packet_claim_profiles: a table claim on a declarative schema file, a different link claim on an embedded schema statement, and a measured zero on a read-only query helper.

Measured fire triple in packet_claim_profiles: a native-constraint claim on a markup page, a different submit-handling claim on a script module, and a measured zero on a markup page without constraints.

crates/codestory-runtime/src/agent/orche.reason: Packet orchestration still recognises holdout schema and router symbols by name when it assembles evidence. Removing them changes which citations a packet keeps, so they are recorded here until the orchestrator selects evidence from indexed structure alone.

crates/codestory-runtime/src/agent/packe.reason: Citation capping keeps holdout entrypoint names so a capped packet retains them. The cap has to learn the same preference from evidence role rather than from the codex-rs and monolog spellings before these can go.

Claim templates are written against holdout call graphs, and the word-part lookups that build them still spell out corpus symbols such as search/parallel and process/input/buffer. Each template needs a source-derived replacement before it can be deleted.
Claim assembly names holdout storage engines when it decides a claim is source-backed. The check has to move to what the indexed file says about itself.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_eviden.reason: The stylesheet carrier lists the words a CSS animation is written with, and one of them collides with a benchmark marker: `animated` is the class name Animate.css and its imitators ship, so a stylesheet whose only anchor is that class would stop closing the animation structure step without it. It goes when a stylesheet requirement is decided from the at-rules the indexer already extracts rather than from a word list.
Evidence-role assignment matches holdout file names to decide whether a citation is a route, a client, or a model. The role has to come from the indexed symbol kind instead.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_flow_r.reason: Flow requirements enumerate holdout DOM and validation identifiers to decide a flow is covered. Deriving the requirement from the question's own terms is the replacement.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_scorin.reason: Citation ranking contains explicit per-file boosts for holdout paths, including path.ends_with checks on corpus file names. This is the largest single benchmark-shaped surface left and the ranking has to be rebuilt on structural signals.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_source.reason: Source-pattern matching keeps holdout identifiers as example words. They are small enough to delete with the callers that supply them, not on their own.

crates/codestory-runtime/src/agent/packe.reason: Sufficiency checks assert that a packet covers named holdout surfaces before it is allowed to answer. The check has to be expressed against the question and the index rather than against corpus spellings. Nine of these markers are gone and thirteen occur less often than they did: sufficiency now decides coverage from a citation's own structure, so the assertions that spelled out corpus symbols were replaced by ones that state the shape a step's evidence has to have.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_terms..reason: Prompt term expansion carries holdout language and API vocabulary. It is the packet-path twin of the search-plan term tables this branch removes and needs the same treatment with packet quality evidence.

crates/codestory-runtime/src/route_cover.reason: The published catalog of web frameworks whose route syntax the indexer extracts. `gin` and `flask` are framework names the indexer independently recognises, not steering toward a holdout, but two of the corpus repositories are named after the frameworks they implement, so the derived identity bans cannot tell the two apart from this file alone. Recorded rather than excused: the catalog has to be derived from the indexer's own declared extractors, and then no framework name is written in the runtime crate at all.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_comman.reason: Command-flow profiling recognises holdout command dispatch symbols by spelling. Replacing that with structural command detection is separate work.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_plan.r.reason: Packet planning still expands questions with holdout symbol and library names. This is the same class of steering as the search-plan tables this branch deletes, and it needs its own change because the packet path has separate quality coverage.

crates/codestory-agent/src/packet_requir.reason: Required-probe selection names holdout languages, files, and APIs so a packet is forced to fetch them. Probes have to be built from the asked question before these can be removed.
